headline: Şəki offers strong educational infrastructure and mountain nature with high affordability.

tags.reason: The area features 16.8% forest cover, mountain terrain at 716 metres elevation, and a nature index of 78 compared to the national median of 52.
Affordability index reaches 94 against the national median of 50, with new apartments priced at AZN 800/m².
The neighbourhood has high park density with 6.8 parks per 10,000 residents and an OSM coverage classified as high.

summary: Şəki is a mountain district with a population of 185,200 and a density of 76 people per km². Educational and healthcare provisions are well above the national median, with 9.13 schools and 2 hospitals per 10,000 residents. The infrastructure index sits at 44, reflecting a paved road share of 0.8% among known surfaces with 73.5% surface unknown. Price data relies on mock confidence values, meaning current real estate figures are demo values.
strengths: High education provision index at 87 with 9.13 schools per 10,000 residents, compared to the national median of 4.14 schools per 10,000 residents (tehsil index 87).
Strong healthcare access with 2 hospitals per 10,000 residents, compared to the national median of 0.75 hospitals per 10,000 residents (sehiyye index 84).
Abundant green spaces with 6.8 parks per 10,000 residents, compared to the national median of 3.89 parks per 10,000 residents (tebiet index 78).
weaknesses: Lower infrastructure rating with an index of 44, compared to the national median of 47 (infrastruktur index 44).
Limited paved road data showing 0.8% paved share of known surfaces with 73.5% surface unknown (paved_pct_of_known 0.8%).
Public transport network relies on 3 rail stations and 53 bus stops, yielding 2.86 bus stops per 10,000 residents against the national median of 0.27 (neqliyyat index 62).
